title: Fault Tree Analysis of an AI Control Protocol

original_idea.body:
# Fault Tree Analysis of an AI Control Protocol

**Problem:** Control safety cases rarely lay out quantitatively the component-failure combinations that lead to an undetected harmful action.

**Direction:** Apply Fault Tree Analysis. Decompose a published protocol into events, populate leaf probabilities from benchmark numbers, and compute the top-event probability plus minimal cut sets. Sensitivity-analyze which leaf most reduces risk.

**Why it matters:** Turns qualitative control safety cases into a quantitative risk model highlighting where to invest. Pure modeling, no compute.

**Relevant context:** FTA aerospace/nuclear standard; control safety-case sketches (arXiv:2501.17315); Ctrl-Z (arXiv:2504.10374).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: FTA turns qualitative control safety cases into quantitative risk models identifying weakest links.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Pure modeling on published numbers; accessible structured-reasoning task.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused FTA of one protocol; depends on decomposition choices and leaf-probability sourcing.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure modeling, no compute; epistemics work labs lack bandwidth to do carefully.

novelty.reasoning: FTA standard; applying it to a control protocol's component numbers plausibly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: FTA mature; control-protocol application plausibly open.
